transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

Possibly, but not yet. A pump that buzzes but moves no water, with a clean filter, is very often a pump that is trying to run but is jammed by something that got past the filter (a coin, hair grip, bra wire or fluff wrapped round the impeller). It can also be a blocked hose further on. Clearing that costs nothing, so it's worth ruling out before blaming the pump. I can't look the code up for your exact model, but on Hoover machines E03 (EO3) usually means the machine couldn't empty in time, which fits what you're seeing. Switch it off and unplug it first. Put towels and a shallow tray down, as some water can still come out of the filter opening. 1. Take the filter out and shine a torch into the hole behind it. You should see a small plastic impeller with vanes. Turn it gently with a finger.
• If something is wrapped round it or wedged in it, remove it, then try a drain or spin-only programme.
• It's normal for it to turn freely with a slight notchy or clicky feel, because these pumps have a magnet inside.
• If it's stiff, won't turn at all, spins with no resistance or has broken vanes, that points to the pump itself.
2. Check the drain hose at the back for kinks or crushing, especially if the machine has been moved recently. Also check where it goes into the standpipe or sink waste. If it joins a sink waste, make sure that spigot isn't blocked; a new sink fitting may still have its blanking disc in. If the impeller turns freely with nothing caught, the hose is clear and it still just buzzes, the drain pump is the likely part. There's a smaller chance of a blockage in the internal sump hose that feeds the pump, which a broken impeller check wouldn't show. Checking a pump is a reasonable repair and usually well worth doing on a machine like this rather than replacing the whole thing. Have a look at the impeller and tell me what you find.
ok did the impeller, spins totally freely no resistance at all, feels like its not even connected. torch shows one fin looks snapped. hose and sink waste both clear. so new pump then?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes, this time I'm fairly confident it's the drain pump. A healthy impeller has a slightly notchy feel because it's coupled to the pump's magnet. One that spins with no resistance at all, plus a snapped fin, means the impeller has broken or come loose from the motor. The buzz is the motor running while the impeller isn't moving any water. Your filter, hose and sink waste are all clear, so a blockage doesn't explain it. What to do next:
1. Order a replacement drain pump. I can't confirm an exact matching part for H3DS4965DACE from here. Use the full model number and the serial number from the label (usually round the door opening) with Hoover's own spares service or a reputable spares supplier, so they can match it for you.
2. When you fit it, have the machine switched off and unplugged. Put towels and a tray down, as there's usually water left in the sump and hose. The pump is typically at the bottom front, behind the filter housing. Some machines reach it from the front, others by tipping the machine back or on its side, so check before you start.
3. Look for the missing piece of fin while the old pump is out. Check inside the old pump housing and the end of the sump hose that feeds it. A loose fragment could jam the new impeller. If you're not comfortable tipping the machine and swapping a part with hoses and a wiring connector, an engineer can do it quickly. A drain pump is one of the cheaper repairs on a washer-dryer, so it's well worth doing rather than replacing the machine. Once the new pump is in, run a drain or spin-only programme and check the floor stays dry.

candidates: Something jammed in the drain pump impeller, just behind the filter (high)
Blocked or kinked drain hose, standpipe or internal sump hose (medium)
